name: Unregistered
description: One of the earliest and most technically raw films to document life without BCI registration in GLMZ — following Priya Dumont-Achebe, an unregistered Shelf resident navigating a city that functionally cannot perceive her, as she attempts to recover her daughter from a corporate medical facility that claims the child doesn't exist. Shot on a $400 Φ budget over eleven months by a collective of anonymous filmmakers, the flat-screen aesthetic was a necessity that became a statement. The film is grainy, brutal, and 94 minutes of sustained dread.
cultural_impact: Considered the founding text of the Unregistered Cinema movement and remains one of the most emotionally cited films among Shelf activist communities, often screened without equipment on salvaged surfaces.
story_hooks: The daughter depicted in the film — now in her twenties — has surfaced and wants to know what happened to her mother after the cameras stopped rolling.
The collective that made the film is still active, and they've been documenting something much larger — they need help getting it out.
The medical facility in the film is still operating under a different name, and it's still doing the same thing.
